title: Expanding Whistleblower Protections for Contractors Act of 2025
official_title: To ensure that whistleblowers, including contractors, are protected from retaliation when a Federal employee orders a reprisal, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Introduced by Rep. Robert Garcia (D-CA-42) with one cosponsor — Rep. James Comer (R-KY-1), Chair of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (the bill's committee of referral). That cross-aisle pairing of the Democratic sponsor with the Republican committee chair drove the House-passed measure per the latest recorded action. The bill extends contractor whistleblower coverage to intelligence community elements within DoD, to state, tribal, and territorial governments acting as contractors, and to personal-services contractors — the intelligence-community pieces and the anti-arbitration waiver clause are the most likely points of Senate pushback, but the sponsor-committee-chair pairing gives the measure a plausible path.
summary: 10 U.S.C. 4701 protects Department of Defense and NASA contractor employees from being fired, demoted, or discriminated against for disclosing evidence of wrongdoing in defense contracts; 41 U.S.C. 4712 does the same for non-defense federal contractors. This bill rewrites both statutes to swap "employee" for a new defined term "protected individual" — which explicitly covers state, tribal, territorial, and personal-services contractors and intelligence-community elements within DoD — expands the covered protected activities to include refusing to obey unlawful orders and disclosing gross mismanagement or gross waste, prohibits executive branch officials from requesting a reprisal, authorizes disciplinary action against officials who do, and bars waiver of the rights, forum, and remedies by any agreement including predispute arbitration.
brief: Rewrites the defense and non-defense federal contractor whistleblower statutes to cover a broader "protected individual" class including intelligence community elements within DoD and state, tribal, and territorial contractors, protects refusal to obey unlawful orders, bars retaliation ordered by executive branch officials, and bans predispute arbitration waiver of the statutory remedies.

top_lines.headline: New "Protected Individual" Class
subs: Replaces "employee" throughout 10 U.S.C. 4701 and 41 U.S.C. 4712 with "protected individual"
Covers contractors, subcontractors, grantees, and subgrantees of DoD, NASA, and (in §4712) the Federal Government
Covers state, DC, tribal, Puerto Rico, Guam, American Samoa, Virgin Islands, N. Mariana Islands, and other territorial governments
Covers political subdivisions, agencies, and instrumentalities of those governments
Covers intelligence community elements within DoD (§4701) and generally (§4712) — defined by 50 U.S.C. 3003
Covers employees, former employees, and personal-services contractors of the above

top_lines.headline: Expanded Protected Activities
subs: Refusing to obey an order that would require violating a law, rule, or regulation
Disclosing gross mismanagement of a DoD or NASA (or Federal) contract or grant
Disclosing gross waste of Department funds or a substantial and specific danger to public health or safety
Disclosing abuse of authority or violation of law related to any contract, subcontract, grant, or subgrant

top_lines.headline: Executive Branch Reprisal-Request Ban
subs: Executive branch officials may not request that a contractor, subcontractor, grantee, or subgrantee engage in a prohibited reprisal
Agencies may propose appropriate disciplinary action against any executive branch official who does
Applies to both DoD/NASA (§4701) and non-defense (§4712) programs

top_lines.headline: Non-Waivable Rights and Anti-Arbitration
subs: Rights, forum, and remedies may not be waived by any public or private agreement
Includes any policy, form, or condition of employment
Explicitly bars predispute arbitration agreements as a waiver mechanism

sections.label: Section 2 — Defense Contractor Employees: Protection From Reprisal (10 U.S.C. 4701)

items.main: Rewrites 10 U.S.C. 4701(a)(1) so a "protected individual" — rather than an "employee" — may not be discharged, demoted, or discriminated against for refusing to obey an unlawful order or disclosing evidence of gross mismanagement, gross waste, abuse of authority, or violation of law related to DoD or NASA contracts, subcontracts, grants, or subgrants, or a substantial and specific danger to public health or safety.
items.detail: The rewrite lists three distinct protected activities: (A) refusing to obey an order that would require the protected individual to violate a law, rule, or regulation related to any contract, subcontract, grant, or subgrant; (B) disclosing to a person or body described in paragraph (2) information the protected individual reasonably believes is evidence of gross mismanagement, gross waste, abuse of authority, or violation of law related to (i) DoD contracts or (ii) NASA contracts; and (iii) a substantial and specific danger to public health or safety.

items.main: Adds a new definition of "protected individual" that includes contractors, subcontractors, grantees, and subgrantees of DoD and NASA — including state, DC, tribal, Puerto Rico, Guam, American Samoa, Virgin Islands, N. Mariana Islands, and other territorial governments, political subdivisions of those governments, and elements of the intelligence community (as defined in 50 U.S.C. 3003) within DoD.
items.detail: The definition also covers employees and former employees of those contractors, subcontractors, grantees, and subgrantees (where the protected activity occurred before termination), and persons performing personal services for DoD or NASA under contractual agreement.

items.main: Prohibits executive branch officials from requesting a reprisal against a contractor, subcontractor, grantee, or subgrantee, and authorizes the head of an executive agency to propose appropriate disciplinary action against any executive branch official who does.
items.detail: Amends 10 U.S.C. 4701(a)(3)(B) to add that it "shall not be within the authority of an executive branch official to request" a prohibited reprisal, and adds new 10 U.S.C. 4701(c)(1)(E) authorizing agency-head disciplinary action against such an official. Also bars waiver of the rights, forum, and remedies by any public or private agreement, policy, form, or condition of employment — including any predispute arbitration agreement.

sections.label: Section 3 — Enhancement of Non-Defense Contractor Protection From Reprisal (41 U.S.C. 4712)

items.main: Applies the same "protected individual" definition, protected activities, executive-branch reprisal-request ban, disciplinary-action authority, and anti-arbitration waiver rule to the non-defense federal contractor whistleblower statute at 41 U.S.C. 4712.
items.detail: The Section 3 amendments parallel Section 2's changes to 10 U.S.C. 4701, applying them to all Federal Government contractors, subcontractors, grantees, and subgrantees (not limited to DoD and NASA). The intelligence-community-element coverage under this section is defined by reference to Section 3 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 3003) without the DoD-only limitation that appears in the Section 2 amendments to 10 U.S.C. 4701.

underreported.section: Section 2(3) — Repeal of 10 U.S.C. 4701(e) and Section 3(4) — Repeal of 41 U.S.C. 4712(f)
underreported.summary: The bill strikes subsection (e) of 10 U.S.C. 4701 and subsection (f) of 41 U.S.C. 4712 and redesignates the following subsections accordingly.
underreported.why_unreported: The section headings describe rewrites of the reprisal-protection rules, but this operative deletion removes an existing subsection of each statute — the text of the deleted subsections is not restated in this bill, so the plain reading of this Act does not show what those subsections previously required.

underreported.summary: The non-defense "protected individual" definition in the amended 41 U.S.C. 4712 covers intelligence-community elements without the "within the Department of Defense" limitation applied in the amended 10 U.S.C. 4701.
underreported.why_unreported: Both sections are captioned as protection-from-reprisal rewrites, but the intelligence-community coverage under Section 3 is broader than under Section 2 — a scope difference not visible from the section labels.

gaps: The bill bars waiver of the rights, forum, and remedies by any predispute arbitration agreement but does not address the enforceability of post-dispute arbitration or settlement agreements that release these claims.

The bill covers intelligence-community elements within DoD (in the amended 10 U.S.C. 4701) but does not address protections for intelligence-community civil employees separately covered by 50 U.S.C. 3234.

The bill authorizes agency heads to propose disciplinary action against executive branch officials who request reprisals but does not require agencies to report the number of such disciplinary proposals or their outcomes.
The bill's rewrites do not address the statute of limitations or the burden-of-proof standard for a protected individual's retaliation claim under the amended sections.

added: "Protected individual" defined in both 10 U.S.C. 4701 and 41 U.S.C. 4712 to include contractors, subcontractors, grantees, subgrantees, state/tribal/territorial governments, political subdivisions, intelligence-community elements, employees and former employees, and personal-services contractors
New protected activity: refusing to obey an order that would require the protected individual to violate a law, rule, or regulation related to any contract, subcontract, grant, or subgrant
New 10 U.S.C. 4701(c)(1)(E) and 41 U.S.C. 4712(c)(1)(E) authority: propose appropriate disciplinary action against any executive branch official who requests a prohibited reprisal
Anti-waiver rule barring public or private agreement (including predispute arbitration) from waiving the rights, forum, and remedies
modified: 10 U.S.C. 4701(a)(1) — rewritten to cover "protected individual" and to list three protected activities (unlawful-order refusal, disclosure of DoD/NASA wrongdoing, disclosure of substantial and specific public health/safety danger)
10 U.S.C. 4701(a)(3)(B) — clarified that executive branch officials have no authority to request a prohibited reprisal
41 U.S.C. 4712(a)(1) — rewritten in parallel to cover Federal Government contracts and "protected individual"
10 U.S.C. 4701(f) and 41 U.S.C. 4712(g) — as redesignated, add the "protected individual" definitional paragraph
